Tip: `git diff main...HEAD -M -- app/themes/default/style.css` shows the move as a rename; `git diff --no-index app/themes/default/style.css app/themes/chapter/style.css` shows how the two themes differ.\n\n**Standards sources to read (read them yourself):**\n- `CLAUDE.md` (hard constraints: relative paths only, never href=\"/...\" or src=\"/...\"; no secrets; argon2; every state-changing form carries a CSRF token; sanitized Markdown; site/ generated; drafts never leave the db; use CONTEXT.md vocabulary; ask before adding a dependency, stack in pyproject.toml fixed)\n- `CONTEXT.md` (the glossary: use its words; the diff adds a \"## Look\" section with Theme and Settings page)\n- `SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md` (items 3, 4, 5, 10 are relevant: CSRF on every POST; editor can't reach admin-only routes; anonymous redirected to login; access control in code)\n- `docs/adr/ADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-002-stack.md`\n- Surrounding-code conventions: compare the new route module with `app/routes/users.py` and `app/routes/media.py` (guards, `_render` helpers, CSRF handling, messages), the new `app/theme.py` with `app/media.py` / `app/content.py` (db access via `db_module.connect()`, docstrings), and the new tests with `tests/test_media.py` / `tests/test_search.py` (test_step<k>_ naming, helpers). Match comment density, naming and idiom of the surrounding code.\n\n**Smell baseline (Fowler, Refactoring ch.3)** — always judgement calls, never hard violations; a documented repo standard overrides them; skip anything tooling enforces:\n- Mysterious Name: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it.\n- Duplicated Code: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape. (Note: the two theme CSS files are deliberately two complete stylesheets because the spec says each theme is ONE CSS file and the published site/style.css must equal the theme's file byte for byte; judge whether the duplication is handled responsibly, e.g. the comments and the test that both themes style the same classes.)\n- Feature Envy: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move it.\n- Data Clumps: the same few fields or params keep travelling together. → bundle them.\n- Primitive Obsession: a primitive standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type.\n- Repeated Switches: the same switch/if-cascade on the same type recurs.\n- Shotgun Surgery: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files.\n- Divergent Change: one module edited for several unrelated reasons.\n- Speculative Generality: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it.\n- Message Chains: long a.b().c().d() navigation.\n- Middle Man: a function that mostly just delegates onward.\n- Refused Bequest: a subclass ignoring most of what it inherits.\n\n**Brief:** Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. (Not to be confused with\napp/settings.py, the configuration read from .env.)\n\"\"\"","originalFile":"\"\"\"The admin-only Settings page (MP2plus F8, issue #23): an Admin picks the\nsite's Theme. The choice is stored in the database, so it survives a\nrestart; the admin console shows it on the next page load, and the public\nsite gets it on the next `cms publish`.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import security\nfrom app import theme as theme_module\nfrom app.guards import require_admin\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin/settings\")\n\nCSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE = \"Your session expired — please try again.\"\nUNKNOWN_THEME_MESSAGE = \"Pick one of the themes listed.\"\n\n\ndef _require_admin_for_settings(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    return require_admin(request, detail=\"Only an Admin can change the site's settings.\")\n\n\ndef _render(request, user, *, saved=None, error=None, status_code=200):\n    csrf_token, new_cookie = security.read_or_mint_csrf(request)\n    response = templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/settings.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Settings\", \"current_user\": user, \"csrf_token\": csrf_token,\n         \"themes\": theme_module.available(), \"selected_theme\": theme_module.selected(),\n         \"saved\": saved, \"error\": error},\n        status_code=status_code,\n    )\n    return security.set_csrf_cookie(response, new_cookie)\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\ndef settings_page(request: Request, user=Depends(_require_admin_for_settings)):\n    return _render(request, user, saved=request.query_params.get(\"saved\"))\n\n\n@router.post(\"\")\ndef save_settings(\n    request: Request,\n    theme: str = Form(\"\"),\n    csrf_token: str = Form(\"\"),\n    user=Depends(_require_admin_for_settings),\n):\n    # Fields default to empty rather than being required, so a POST missing\n    # its token gets this page's message, not a 422.\n    if not security.verify_csrf(csrf_token, request.cookies.get(security.CSRF_COOKIE)):\n        return _render(request, user, error=CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE, status_code=403)\n    try:\n        theme_module.select(theme)\n    except theme_module.UnknownTheme:\n        return _render(request, user, error=UNKNOWN_THEME_MESSAGE, status_code=400)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/settings?saved=theme\", status_code=303)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":7,"newStart":1,"newLines":8,"lines":[" \"\"\"The admin-only Settings page (MP2plus F8, issue #23): an Admin picks the"," site's Theme. The choice is stored in the database, so it survives a"," restart; the admin console shows it on the next page load, and the public","-site gets it on the next `cms publish`.","+site gets it on the next `cms publish`. (Not to be confused with","+app/settings.py, the configuration read from .env.)"," \"\"\""," from __future__ import annotations"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"4a15b7ba-9575-45c9-8b11-6baf6c8e73a9","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"46a8d74b-d860-4909-a43f-d4dbcfcc3476","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"0008ac86-4a00-4c89-8a62-5971452a5ff3","version":"2.1.305","gitBranch":"mp2plus-f8"}

{"parentUuid":"6fcc4947-786c-4c55-8bdf-ddb73f52dc8a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgEvpenymM2XvmYKb4B2J","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01N1Vs1coi3hdUuEC1xXshAy","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\0008ac86-4a00-4c89-8a62-5971452a5ff3\\scratchpad\\findings.md","content":"## /code-review findings for T23 (F8 Switchable theme), and how each was resolved\n\nTwo-axis review of `main...mp2plus-f8` at 6ed8624, run as two separate reviewers:\n- **Standards:** CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md and the ADRs, plus a fixed Fowler smell baseline.\n- **Spec:** issue #23's acceptance checklist, the build prompt, and the decisions made before coding.\n\nThe fixes marked *Fixed* are pushed to this branch after this comment.\n\n### Standards: no hard violations\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| S1 | Duplicated Code (judgement call). The two themes are two complete stylesheets by design: a Theme is one file, and `site/style.css` must equal it byte for byte. But `test_step1_each_theme_styles_every_class_the_other_does` compares class *names* only, so a layout value fixed in one file and not the other still passes. | **Fixed.** The test's comment now says what it doesn't check. The layout itself is covered by a new step 5 test of the exported site at 390 px in both themes (P8). |\n| S2 | Hidden contract. The first line of each stylesheet's header becomes its description on the Settings page, and only `app/theme.py` says so. | **Fixed.** Both CSS headers now say that line 1 is the Settings page description. |\n| S3 | \"settings\" means three things: `app/settings.py` (the `.env` configuration), the `settings` table, and the Settings page. | **Fixed.** The docstring in `app/routes/admin_settings.py` now tells them apart. CONTEXT.md's *Settings page* entry already does. |\n| S4 | `tests/test_access_control_sweep.py` claims to cover \"every admin route\", but its lists have neither `/admin/settings` nor `/admin/media` (missing since T21). | **Not changed.** That file existed at `mp2plus-base`, so this PR leaves it alone. `tests/test_theme.py` checks the Editor 403 and the anonymous redirect to login for both GET and POST. S1 comes next and replaces the hand-typed lists with a matrix built from the router. |\n| S5 | `CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE` is now defined in a third module. | **Not changed.** This follows the existing one-constant-per-module pattern. Merging the copies would touch four modules unrelated to F8. |\n| S6 | Speculative Generality / Primitive Obsession (minor): a key/value `settings` table that holds one value, and `stylesheet(name=None)`. | **Not changed.** The spec asks for \"a settings table\", and F7 shares the same page. Both are small and documented. |\n\n### Spec: all 6 steps and the 3 decisions made before coding are implemented; nothing looks implemented wrongly\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| P1 | Issue #23 is still open, and the commit says \"Part of #23\". | **By design for P1.** This findings comment comes first. The fix commit then ends with `Closes #23`, and merging this PR closes the issue. |\n| P2 | The schema changed (a new `settings` table), so the user must be told `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`. | **Resolved in the hand-off to the user.** The command is given with a back-up-first warning, because the real `cms.db` holds the client site. The table is created on first open (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), so no re-seed is needed. `scripts/seed_demo.py` runs clean from `.env.example` values on a fresh database (checked). |\n| P3 | `.env.example` only gets a comment. | **Kept.** No environment variable was added: the Theme is a database setting. The comment says where it is set. |\n| P4 | Unrequested: a stored Theme whose folder was later removed falls back to `default`. | **Kept.** Without it, `/style.css` returns a 500 error and `cms publish` crashes, which would break step 3. It is small and tested. |\n| P5 | Unrequested: each description is parsed from the first comment line of the theme's CSS. | **Kept.** This keeps a Theme to one file, with no separate list of names. It is now documented in the CSS (S2). |\n| P6 | `test_step2_the_settings_page_fits_a_390px_phone` checks layout. | **Kept as step 2.** The manual's *walk* is done at 1280 and 390 px, so step 2's Settings page has to work at 390. |\n| P7 | The step 3 fallback test and the step 1 class test go beyond their steps. | **Kept.** The fallback is what keeps step 3's \"every page's relative stylesheet link still works\" true. The class test makes sure the second theme is a complete one (step 1). |\n| P8 | The step 5 tests load the dev server's preview, not the exported `site/`. | **Fixed.** The new `test_step5_the_published_site_fits_a_390px_phone` publishes into a temporary `site/` and serves it the way `python -m http.server` does. It checks the home page and a post in both themes in Chromium. The old test is renamed `test_step5_the_dev_server_preview_fits_a_390px_phone`. Both mutations tried turn the new test red: publish writing the default theme, and chapter's `pre` losing `max-width`. |\n\n**Evidence at 6ed8624:**\n- `tests/test_theme.py`: 26 passed.\n- Full suite: 393 passed. The 367 tests that existed before are unchanged.\n- `check_submission.py --stage 2`: 22/22.\n- Judge-style walk: 83/83. It switches the theme, restarts the dev-server process, publishes and compares `site/style.css` with the theme's file, switches back, checks both themes at 1280 and 390, and replays the POST without its token.\n- Mutations: 23/23 killed.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1055,"cache_read_input_tokens":279159,"output_tokens":4234,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1771},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1055,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":4234,"cache_read_input_tokens":279159,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1055,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1055},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01N1Vs1coi3hdUuEC1xXshAy":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\0008ac86-4a00-4c89-8a62-5971452a5ff3\\scratchpad\\findings.md","content":"## /code-review findings for T23 (F8 Switchable theme), and how each was resolved\n\nTwo-axis review of `main...mp2plus-f8` at 6ed8624, run as two separate reviewers:\n- **Standards:** CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md and the ADRs, plus a fixed Fowler smell baseline.\n- **Spec:** issue #23's acceptance checklist, the build prompt, and the decisions made before coding.\n\nThe fixes marked *Fixed* are pushed to this branch after this comment.\n\n### Standards: no hard violations\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| S1 | Duplicated Code (judgement call). The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>The theme switch works. The full test suite passes (397 tests, including the browser tests), the stage-2 submission checker scores 22/22, and a smoke test on a copy of your real `cms.db` behaved correctly: switching to chapter and publishing writes chapter's file as `site/style.css`, and switching back restores default's. I found no bug that breaks normal use. The 13 findings below are edge cases, gaps in test coverage and cleanup. Only the first one was reproduced; the rest come from reading the code.\n\n- **Finding 1, reproduced:** restoring a database file that has no `settings` table while the server is running makes `/style.css` return a 500 error. The app does not re-check the schema of a file it has already opened, so every admin and preview page loses its styling until a restart. Your real `cms.db` already has the table, so this only bites with an older backup.\n- **Before you deploy:** your local `site/style.css` is still the old pre-T23 stylesheet. Run `cms publish` again before `cms deploy`.\n\n```json\n[\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/theme.py\",\n    \"line\": 58,\n    \"summary\": \"selected() lets any sqlite error escape, and /style.css (which every admin and preview page links) calls it on every request, so one database problem leaves the whole console without styling.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Reproduced: start the app, then copy a database file with no `settings` table over cms.db while it runs (e.g. restoring a backup made before T23). The app has already marked that path as initialised in _schema_ready, so the table is never created. GET /style.css then returns 500 'no such table: settings', every admin page renders unstyled, and /admin/settings returns 500 until a restart. A missing row already means 'default'; a missing table or other sqlite error could fall back to DEFAULT_THEME too.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/publish.py\",\n    \"line\": 140,\n    \"summary\": \"render_site deletes and recreates site/ before it works out the theme stylesheet, so if that lookup or the copy fails, an empty site/ is left behind that `cms deploy` will push.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"theme_module.stylesheet() raises (sqlite 'database is locked' after the 5 s timeout, or the theme file is missing). `cms publish` crashes after shutil.rmtree(out) and out.mkdir(), leaving an empty site/. `cms deploy` only checks settings.SITE.exists() (cli.py:45), so it pushes an empty gh-pages and the live site stops working. Working out the stylesheet path before the rmtree avoids this.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/theme.py\",\n    \"line\": 58,\n    \"summary\": \"The fallback returns DEFAULT_THEME without checking that app/themes/default/style.css exists, so the 'removed theme falls back' safety net fails if the default folder itself is renamed or removed.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Rename app/themes/default to e.g. app/themes/indigo (CONTEXT.md only names it). With no stored row, selected() still returns 'default', stylesheet() builds a path that doesn't exist, /style.css raises FileNotFoundError (500), and `cms publish` crashes inside shutil.copyfile after site/ has been deleted.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/theme.py\",\n    \"line\": 81,\n    \"summary\": \"stylesheet(name) joins `name` into a path without checking it against names(); only select() validates. Any future caller that passes request input can read files outside app/themes/.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"A later 'preview a theme' feature calls theme_module.stylesheet(request.query_params['theme']). Then ?theme=../../site or ?theme=..%2F.. resolves to THEMES_DIR/../../&lt;x&gt;/style.css, which reads and serves files outside app/themes/. Today the only caller with an explicit name is available(), which passes names from names(), so this is a trap for future code, not a live bug.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"templates/admin/settings.html\",\n    \"line\": 6,\n    \"summary\": \"The success banner says the public site changes on the next `cms publish`, but publish only rewrites the local site/; the live GitHub Pages site changes only after `cms deploy` as well.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"An Admin (the client) saves 'chapter', runs `cms publish`, and expects the deployed site to be black and gold. It still shows indigo until someone also runs `cms deploy`. The docstring at app/routes/admin_settings.py:3-4 makes the same claim.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/routes/public.py\",\n    \"line\": 32,\n    \"summary\": \"/style.css now serves different bytes at the same URL over time but sends no Cache-Control or validators, so the 'a switch shows on the next page load' promise relies on each browser's default caching.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Before this change the response could not change while the server ran, so caching didn't matter. Now any cache that applies its own freshness rules (a proxy, an extension, a back/forward cache restore) can keep the previous theme's CSS after an Admin saves a new one. Sending `Cache-Control: no-cache` would guarantee the next load fetches the selected theme.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"tests/test_access_control_sweep.py\",\n    \"line\": 49,\n    \"summary\": \"The access-control sweep's docstring claims every admin route, but its lists still leave out /admin/settings (GET and POST), and /admin/media too.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"A later refactor swaps _require_admin_for_settings for require_editor_or_admin, or drops the CSRF check on the POST. The cross-cutting sweep stays green, and only test_theme.py would notice. This gap was noted as S4 on PR #24 and left unchanged.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"tests/test_theme.py\",\n    \"line\": 73,\n    \"summary\": \"test_step1 requires each theme folder to contain exactly ['style.css'], so an OS metadata file makes it fail.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Opening app/themes/default in macOS Finder (.gitignore already lists .DS_Store) or in Windows Explorer with thumbnails on (Thumbs.db / desktop.ini) adds a file. The test then fails with ['.DS_Store', 'style.css'] != ['style.css'] even though names() and the app are fine. Checking that the folder has a style.css and no other .css files would be enough.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/theme.py\",\n    \"line\": 49,\n    \"summary\": \"Every /style.css request now opens a new SQLite connection, runs a query, globs the themes folder and reads the file from disk. The Settings page globs twice and reads every theme file in full just to get one comment line each.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Every page view on the dev server (admin or preview) pays a DB connection plus directory scan for a file that changes only when an Admin presses Save. That is a small cost locally but grows with request rate. A cheaper option: keep the selected theme's bytes in memory and refresh them in select(), or cache them by (selected name, file mtime). available() could read just the first line of each file.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/themes/chapter/style.css\",\n    \"line\": 1,\n    \"summary\": \"The chapter theme is a near-full 480-line copy of default that differs in about 40 declarations. The parity test compares class names only, so a layout fix made in one file silently drifts from the other.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Someone fixes `.content-list__actions` wrapping in app/themes/default/style.css, the class names stay the same, test_step1_each_theme_styles_every_class_the_other_does passes, and chapter keeps the bug. The step-5 phone-width tests only cover the home page and one post. A fix at the root: keep a shared layout file plus a per-theme tokens/overrides file, and join them into the one served or exported style.css. That conflicts with 'each one CSS file', so a test that diffs the two files outside their token and override blocks would be the minimum guard.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/themes/chapter/style.css\",\n    \"line\": 20,\n    \"summary\": \"--on-accent is defined in chapter's light (line 20) and dark (line 54) blocks but never used, because chapter's buttons use --gold and --ink instead.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"The dead token suggests it controls button text. Someone tweaking chapter's button contrast edits --on-accent and nothing changes.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/routes/admin_settings.py\",\n    \"line\": 21,\n    \"summary\": \"CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE is now copied word for word into a third route module (users.py:20, media.py:19), along with another _require_admin_for_* and _render CSRF-cookie wrapper.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Changing the wording of the expired-session message, or how the CSRF cookie is reissued, now means editing three modules. Missing one gives inconsistent messages, and tests assert on the 'session expired' substring. Moving the constant to app/security.py would let every route import one copy.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"CLAUDE.md\",\n    \"line\": 1,\n    \"summary\": \"This breaks the CLAUDE.md rule 'Before a commit that closes a ticket: post the `/code-review` findings, and how each was resolved, as a comment on that issue': issue #23's only comment is a link, and the findings themselves are on PR #24.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Commit 21917c0 ends 'Closes #23', but the issue #23 comment reads only 'Code-review findings for this issue, and how each was resolved, are on PR #24: &lt;link&gt;'. Anyone reading the issue, which is what the rule targets, sees no findings unless they follow the link, and the record breaks if the PR comment is edited or the PR is deleted.\"\n  }\n]\n```</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>141175</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>38</tool_uses><duration_ms>658277</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

Only the first one was reproduced; the rest come from reading the code.\n\n- **Finding 1, reproduced:** restoring a database file that has no `settings` table while the server is running makes `/style.css` return a 500 error. The app does not re-check the schema of a file it has already opened, so every admin and preview page loses its styling until a restart. Your real `cms.db` already has the table, so this only bites with an older backup.\n- **Before you deploy:** your local `site/style.css` is still the old pre-T23 stylesheet. Run `cms publish` again before `cms deploy`.\n\n```json\n[\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/theme.py\",\n    \"line\": 58,\n    \"summary\": \"selected() lets any sqlite error escape, and /style.css (which every admin and preview page links) calls it on every request, so one database problem leaves the whole console without styling.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Reproduced: start the app, then copy a database file with no `settings` table over cms.db while it runs (e.g. restoring a backup made before T23). The app has already marked that path as initialised in _schema_ready, so the table is never created. GET /style.css then returns 500 'no such table: settings', every admin page renders unstyled, and /admin/settings returns 500 until a restart. A missing row already means 'default'; a missing table or other sqlite error could fall back to DEFAULT_THEME too.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/publish.py\",\n    \"line\": 140,\n    \"summary\": \"render_site deletes and recreates site/ before it works out the theme stylesheet, so if that lookup or the copy fails, an empty site/ is left behind that `cms deploy` will push.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"theme_module.stylesheet() raises (sqlite 'database is locked' after the 5 s timeout, or the theme file is missing). `cms publish` crashes after shutil.rmtree(out) and out.mkdir(), leaving an empty site/. `cms deploy` only checks settings.SITE.exists() (cli.py:45), so it pushes an empty gh-pages and the live site stops working. Working out the stylesheet path before the rmtree avoids this.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/theme.py\",\n    \"line\": 58,\n    \"summary\": \"The fallback returns DEFAULT_THEME without checking that app/themes/default/style.css exists, so the 'removed theme falls back' safety net fails if the default folder itself is renamed or removed.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Rename app/themes/default to e.g. app/themes/indigo (CONTEXT.md only names it). With no stored row, selected() still returns 'default', stylesheet() builds a path that doesn't exist, /style.css raises FileNotFoundError (500), and `cms publish` crashes inside shutil.copyfile after site/ has been deleted.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/theme.py\",\n    \"line\": 81,\n    \"summary\": \"stylesheet(name) joins `name` into a path without checking it against names(); only select() validates. Any future caller that passes request input can read files outside app/themes/.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"A later 'preview a theme' feature calls theme_module.stylesheet(request.query_params['theme']). Then ?theme=../../site or ?theme=..%2F.. resolves to THEMES_DIR/../../&lt;x&gt;/style.css, which reads and serves files outside app/themes/. Today the only caller with an explicit name is available(), which passes names from names(), so this is a trap for future code, not a live bug.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"templates/admin/settings.html\",\n    \"line\": 6,\n    \"summary\": \"The success banner says the public site changes on the next `cms publish`, but publish only rewrites the local site/; the live GitHub Pages site changes only after `cms deploy` as well.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"An Admin (the client) saves 'chapter', runs `cms publish`, and expects the deployed site to be black and gold. Now any cache that applies its own freshness rules (a proxy, an extension, a back/forward cache restore) can keep the previous theme's CSS after an Admin saves a new one. Sending `Cache-Control: no-cache` would guarantee the next load fetches the selected theme.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"tests/test_access_control_sweep.py\",\n    \"line\": 49,\n    \"summary\": \"The access-control sweep's docstring claims every admin route, but its lists still leave out /admin/settings (GET and POST), and /admin/media too.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"A later refactor swaps _require_admin_for_settings for require_editor_or_admin, or drops the CSRF check on the POST. The cross-cutting sweep stays green, and only test_theme.py would notice. This gap was noted as S4 on PR #24 and left unchanged.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"tests/test_theme.py\",\n    \"line\": 73,\n    \"summary\": \"test_step1 requires each theme folder to contain exactly ['style.css'], so an OS metadata file makes it fail.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Opening app/themes/default in macOS Finder (.gitignore already lists .DS_Store) or in Windows Explorer with thumbnails on (Thumbs.db / desktop.ini) adds a file. The test then fails with ['.DS_Store', 'style.css'] != ['style.css'] even though names() and the app are fine. Checking that the folder has a style.css and no other .css files would be enough.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/theme.py\",\n    \"line\": 49,\n    \"summary\": \"Every /style.css request now opens a new SQLite connection, runs a query, globs the themes folder and reads the file from disk. {"parentUuid":"a028dbd3-057a-44cf-9ce3-8cccc4ee147e","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"ca3ab0bd-7669-4f66-8f1f-310281f79d31","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UNN4UHXsYERUu9TckLDEMb","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\theme.py has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"ccc0d49c-98b7-44eb-9764-9a6ff795e89e","timestamp":"2026-10-21T07:08:29.045Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\theme.py","oldString":"import re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass","newString":"import re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass","originalFile":"\"\"\"The site's Theme (see CONTEXT.md): which stylesheet, of the ones in\napp/themes/<name>/style.css, the admin console and the Static export use.\n\nAn Admin picks it on the Settings page. The choice is a row in the\ndatabase's `settings` table and is read again on every use, so a switch\nreaches the next page load and the next `cms publish` with no restart.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import db as db_module\n\nTHEMES_DIR = Path(__file__).with_name(\"themes\")\nDEFAULT_THEME = \"default\"\nSETTING_KEY = \"theme\"\n\n# A stylesheet's description is the first line of its opening /* comment */.\nDESCRIPTION_RE = re.compile(r\"\\s*/\\*\\s*(.*?)\\s*(?:\\*/|\\n)\")\n\n\nclass UnknownTheme(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"A theme name with no app/themes/<name>/style.css.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Theme:\n    name: str\n    description: str\n\n\ndef names() -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Every theme's name, the default first, then A to Z.\"\"\"\n    found = [path.parent.name for path in THEMES_DIR.glob(\"*/style.css\")]\n    return sorted(found, key=lambda name: (name != DEFAULT_THEME, name))\n\n\ndef available() -> list[Theme]:\n    \"\"\"Every theme, in names() order, for the Settings page.\"\"\"\n    themes = []\n    for name in names():\n        match = DESCRIPTION_RE.match(stylesheet(name).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        themes.append(Theme(name, match.group(1) if match else \"\"))\n    return themes\n\n\ndef selected() -> str:\n    \"\"\"The stored theme, or the default when none is stored yet or the\n    stored one's folder has since been removed.\"\"\"\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        row = conn.execute(\"SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key = ?\",\n                           (SETTING_KEY,)).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n    return row[\"value\"] if row and row[\"value\"] in names() else DEFAULT_THEME\n\n\ndef select(name: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Store `name` as the site's theme. Raises UnknownTheme if there is no\n    such theme, so only a real folder's name is ever stored.\"\"\"\n    if name not in names():\n        raise UnknownTheme(name)\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO settings (key, value) VALUES (?, ?) \"\n            \"ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value\",\n            (SETTING_KEY, name),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef stylesheet(name: str | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"The style.css file of theme `name`, or of the selected theme. Callers\n    copy its bytes as they are, so site/style.css matches the file exactly.\"\"\"\n    return THEMES_DIR / (name or selected()) / \"style.css\"","newString":"def stylesheet() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"The selected theme's style.css. Callers copy its bytes as they are,\n    so site/style.css matches the file exactly.\"\"\"\n    return _file(selected())","originalFile":"\"\"\"The site's Theme (see CONTEXT.md): which stylesheet, of the ones in\napp/themes/<name>/style.css, the admin console and the Static export use.\n\nAn Admin picks it on the Settings page. The choice is a row in the\ndatabase's `settings` table and is read again on every use, so a switch\nreaches the next page load and the next `cms publish` with no restart.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import db as db_module\n\nTHEMES_DIR = Path(__file__).with_name(\"themes\")\nDEFAULT_THEME = \"default\"\nSETTING_KEY = \"theme\"\n\n# A stylesheet's description is the first line of its opening /* comment */.\nDESCRIPTION_RE = re.compile(r\"\\s*/\\*\\s*(.*?)\\s*(?:\\*/|\\n)\")\n\n\nclass UnknownTheme(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"A theme name with no app/themes/<name>/style.css.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Theme:\n    name: str\n    description: str\n\n\ndef _file(name: str) -> Path:\n    return THEMES_DIR / name / \"style.css\"\n\n\ndef names() -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Every theme's name, the default first, then A to Z.\"\"\"\n    found = [path.parent.name for path in THEMES_DIR.glob(\"*/style.css\")]\n    return sorted(found, key=lambda name: (name != DEFAULT_THEME, name))\n\n\ndef available() -> list[Theme]:\n    \"\"\"Every theme, in names() order, for the Settings page.\"\"\"\n    themes = []\n    for name in names():\n        match = DESCRIPTION_RE.match(_file(name).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        themes.append(Theme(name, match.group(1) if match else \"\"))\n    return themes\n\n\ndef selected() -> str:\n    \"\"\"The stored theme, or the default when none is stored yet or the\n    stored one's folder has since been removed.\"\"\"\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        row = conn.execute(\"SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key = ?\",\n                           (SETTING_KEY,)).fetchone()\n    except sqlite3.OperationalError:\n        # No settings table: a backup from before it existed, copied over\n        # the database while the server runs. Every page still gets styled.\n        row = None\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n    return row[\"value\"] if row and row[\"value\"] in names() else DEFAULT_THEME\n\n\ndef select(name: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Store `name` as the site's theme. Raises UnknownTheme if there is no\n    such theme, so only a real folder's name is ever stored.\"\"\"\n    if name not in names():\n        raise UnknownTheme(name)\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO settings (key, value) VALUES (?, ?) \"\n            \"ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value\",\n            (SETTING_KEY, name),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef stylesheet(name: str | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"The style.css file of theme `name`, or of the selected theme. Callers\n    copy its bytes as they are, so site/style.css matches the file exactly.\"\"\"\n    return THEMES_DIR / (name or selected()) / \"style.css\"\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":84,"oldLines":7,"newStart":84,"newLines":7,"lines":["         conn.close()"," "," ","-def stylesheet(name: str | None = None) -> Path:","-    \"\"\"The style.css file of theme `name`, or of the selected theme. {"parentUuid":"3f33e315-681b-4b07-947f-2ebbb31b9366","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"ca3ab0bd-7669-4f66-8f1f-310281f79d31","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01F9MzpShp4SbcopdefufPnq","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\publish.py has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"6b5d0bab-ff75-4d8c-b4f9-e9d379d1ac58","timestamp":"2026-10-21T07:08:30.034Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\publish.py","oldString":"    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    # The selected Theme's file, byte for byte, under the one name every\n    # page links: switching themes changes the file, never the links.\n    shutil.copyfile(theme_module.stylesheet(), out / \"style.css\")","newString":"    out = out or settings.SITE\n    # The selected Theme's file, byte for byte, under the one name every\n    # page links: switching themes changes the file, never the links. Read\n    # before site/ is cleared, so a failure here leaves the last export whole.\n    css = theme_module.stylesheet().read_bytes()\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_bytes(css)","originalFile":"\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n     That includes links written in a body: render_markdown(..., to_root=...)\n     rewrites \"/contact-us.html\" and \"media/logo.png\" for the file it lands in.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content as content_module\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app import theme as theme_module\nfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown, render_text\n\n# search.html's one script, which searches site/search-index.json.\nSEARCH_JS = Path(__file__).with_name(\"search.js\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n# The most characters of a body that search.html shows under a result's title.\nEXCERPT_LENGTH = 160\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef nav_items(prefix: str = \"\") -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Published Pages, as relative (title, href) links for the public\n    site's nav. `prefix` relocates the link for a page nested one\n    directory deep (e.g. \"../\" from site/posts/*.html) — a draft Page\n    never appears here.\"\"\"\n    return [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"{prefix}{page['slug']}.html\"}\n            for page in _exportable_pages()]\n\n\ndef _exportable_pages() -> list:\n    # The editor already refuses reserved slugs; this also covers rows saved\n    # before that check existed, so a Page can never overwrite site/index.html.\n    return [page for page in content_module.list_published(\"page\")\n            if not content_module.reserved_slug_reason(\"page\", page[\"slug\"])]\n\n\ndef _date(item) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The calendar day an item was created, e.g. \"2026-10-07\".\"\"\"\n    return item[\"created_at\"][:10]\n\n\ndef home_html() -> str:\n    \"\"\"The home page (feed of published Posts), as written to site/index.html.\"\"\"\n    posts = content_module.list_published(\"post\")\n    return environment().get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n        title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[\n            {\"title\": post[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\",\n             \"date\": _date(post)} for post in posts\n        ],\n        css_path=\"style.css\", home_path=\"index.html\", nav_items=nav_items(),\n    )\n\n\ndef search_html() -> str:\n    \"\"\"The search page, as written to site/search.html; its script is\n    site/search.js.\"\"\"\n    return environment().get_template(\"public/search.html\").render(\n        title=\"Search\", site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE,\n        css_path=\"style.css\", home_path=\"index.html\", nav_items=nav_items(),\n    )\n\n\ndef search_index_json() -> str:\n    \"\"\"site/search-index.json: the title, URL and a plain-text excerpt of\n    every published Post and Page, for search.html's script to search. Each\n    URL is relative to the site root, where search.html is.\"\"\"\n    items = [(post, f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\")\n             for post in content_module.list_published(\"post\")]\n    items += [(page, f\"{page['slug']}.html\") for page in _exportable_pages()]\n    return json.dumps([\n        {\"title\": item[\"title\"], \"url\": url, \"excerpt\": _excerpt(item[\"body_md\"])}\n        for item, url in items\n    ], ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)\n\n\ndef _excerpt(body_md: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The start of a body as plain text, EXCERPT_LENGTH characters or fewer\n    with the \"…\" that ends it when anything was cut. The cut falls at a word\n    break, unless the text has none to fall at.\"\"\"\n    text = render_text(body_md)\n    if len(text) <= EXCERPT_LENGTH:\n        return text\n    head = text[:EXCERPT_LENGTH]\n    cut = head.rsplit(\" \", 1)[0] if \" \" in head else head[:-1]\n    return (cut.rstrip(\" .,;:\") or cut) + \"…\"\n\n\ndef post_html(post) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A published Post, as written to site/posts/<slug>.html — one directory\n    deep, so every shared link climbs a level.\"\"\"\n    return _detail_html(\"public/post.html\", \"post\", post, prefix=\"../\")\n\n\ndef page_html(page) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A published Page, as written to site/<slug>.html.\"\"\"\n    return _detail_html(\"public/page.html\", \"page\", page, prefix=\"\")\n\n\ndef _detail_html(template_name: str, item_key: str, item, *, prefix: str) -> str:\n    return environment().get_template(template_name).render(\n        title=item[\"title\"], site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE,\n        **{item_key: item}, date=_date(item),\n        body_html=render_markdown(item[\"body_md\"], to_root=prefix),\n        css_path=f\"{prefix}style.css\", home_path=f\"{prefix}index.html\",\n        nav_items=nav_items(prefix=prefix),\n    )\n\n\ndef _write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    # Explicit UTF-8: the pages declare <meta charset=\"utf-8\">, and the\n    # platform default (cp1252 on Windows) can't encode an emoji at all.\n    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    # The selected Theme's file, byte for byte, under the one name every\n    # page links: switching themes changes the file, never the links.\n    shutil.copyfile(theme_module.stylesheet(), out / \"style.css\")\n    _write(out / \"index.html\", home_html())\n    _write(out / \"search.html\", search_html())\n    _write(out / \"search.js\", SEARCH_JS)\n    _write(out / \"search-index.json\", search_index_json())\n\n    posts_dir = out / \"posts\"\n    posts_dir.mkdir()\n    for post in content_module.list_published(\"post\"):\n        _write(posts_dir / f\"{post['slug']}.html\", post_html(post))\n    for page in _exportable_pages():\n        _write(out / f\"{page['slug']}.html\", page_html(page))\n\n    # Every file in media/ is meant to be public; Posts show them through\n    # their Media library snippets.\n    if settings.MEDIA.is_dir():\n        shutil.copytree(settings.MEDIA, out / \"media\")\n\n    return out\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":132,"oldLines":12,"newStart":132,"newLines":14,"lines":[" "," def render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:","     out = out or settings.SITE","+    # The selected Theme's file, byte for byte, under the one name every","+    # page links: switching themes changes the file, never the links. Read","+    # before site/ is cleared, so a failure here leaves the last export whole.","+    css = theme_module.stylesheet().read_bytes()","     if out.exists():","         shutil.rmtree(out)","     out.mkdir(parents=True)","-    # The selected Theme's file, byte for byte, under the one name every","-    # page links: switching themes changes the file, never the links.","-    shutil.copyfile(theme_module.stylesheet(), out / \"style.css\")","+    (out / \"style.css\").write_bytes(css)","     _write(out / \"index.html\", home_html())","     _write(out / \"search.html\", search_html())","     _write(out / \"search.js\", SEARCH_JS)"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"3f33e315-681b-4b07-947f-2ebbb31b9366","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"46a8d74b-d860-4909-a43f-d4dbcfcc3476","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"0008ac86-4a00-4c89-8a62-5971452a5ff3","version":"2.1.305","gitBranch":"mp2plus-f8"}

The admin console links this file too.\n    return Response(theme_module.stylesheet().read_bytes(), media_type=\"text/css\")","newString":"    # The selected Theme, read per request: a switch on the Settings page\n    # shows on the next page load. The admin console links this file too.\n    # no-cache: the same URL serves new bytes after a switch.\n    return Response(theme_module.stylesheet().read_bytes(), media_type=\"text/css\",\n                    headers={\"Cache-Control\": \"no-cache\"})","originalFile":"\"\"\"The public site, served live by the dev server at the same paths the static\nexport writes (index.html, posts/<slug>.html, <slug>.html, search.html with\nits search.js and search-index.json, and style.css, the selected Theme). Both\nrender through app.publish and app.theme, so the local preview and the\ndeployed site can't drift.\nOnly published content is ever served; a draft's URL is a 404.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException\nfrom fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, Response\n\nfrom app import content as content_module\nfrom app import theme as theme_module\nfrom app.publish import (\n    SEARCH_JS, home_html, page_html, post_html, search_html, search_index_json,\n)\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\n\n\n@router.get(\"/\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n@router.get(\"/index.html\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\ndef home():\n    return home_html()\n\n\n@router.get(\"/style.css\")\ndef style_css():\n    # The selected Theme, read per request: a switch on the Settings page\n    # shows on the next page load. The choice is stored in the database, so it survives a\nrestart; the admin console shows it on the next page load, and the public\nsite gets it on the next `cms publish`. (Not to be confused with\napp/settings.py, the configuration read from .env.)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import security\nfrom app import theme as theme_module\nfrom app.guards import require_admin\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin/settings\")\n\nCSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE = \"Your session expired — please try again.\"\nUNKNOWN_THEME_MESSAGE = \"Pick one of the themes listed.\"\n\n\ndef _require_admin_for_settings(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    return require_admin(request, detail=\"Only an Admin can change the site's settings.\")\n\n\ndef _render(request, user, *, saved=None, error=None, status_code=200):\n    csrf_token, new_cookie = security.read_or_mint_csrf(request)\n    response = templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/settings.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Settings\", \"current_user\": user, \"csrf_token\": csrf_token,\n         \"themes\": theme_module.available(), \"selected_theme\": theme_module.selected(),\n         \"saved\": saved, \"error\": error},\n        status_code=status_code,\n    )\n    return security.set_csrf_cookie(response, new_cookie)\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\ndef settings_page(request: Request, user=Depends(_require_admin_for_settings)):\n    return _render(request, user, saved=request.query_params.get(\"saved\"))\n\n\n@router.post(\"\")\ndef save_settings(\n    request: Request,\n    theme: str = Form(\"\"),\n    csrf_token: str = Form(\"\"),\n    user=Depends(_require_admin_for_settings),\n):\n    # Fields default to empty rather than being required, so a POST missing\n    # its token gets this page's message, not a 422.\n    if not security.verify_csrf(csrf_token, request.cookies.get(security.CSRF_COOKIE)):\n        return _render(request, user, error=CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE, status_code=403)\n    try:\n        theme_module.select(theme)\n    except theme_module.UnknownTheme:\n        return _render(request, user, error=UNKNOWN_THEME_MESSAGE, status_code=400)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/settings?saved=theme\", status_code=303)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":7,"newStart":1,"newLines":8,"lines":[" \"\"\"The admin-only Settings page (MP2plus F8, issue #23): an Admin picks the"," site's Theme. {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"0008ac86-4a00-4c89-8a62-5971452a5ff3","hash":"6962becd659b7ad149510e5c56a682d870698b31d1ad1bf70213743ec066705c","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01UWPhF5mGodXvrsSWoVWzTJ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\0008ac86-4a00-4c89-8a62-5971452a5ff3\\scratchpad\\findings2.md","content":"## /code-review round 2 for T23 (F8): findings and how each was resolved\n\nThis round was a separate `/code-review` of the branch at 21917c0, asked to \"make sure everything's working right\". It found:\n- 397 tests pass, and the checker is 22/22.\n- A smoke test on a *copy* of the real `cms.db` worked: switching to chapter and publishing wrote chapter's file as `site/style.css`, and switching back restored the default's.\n- No bug that breaks normal use. It reported 13 edge cases, test gaps and cleanups; only #1 was reproduced.\n\nThe fixes marked *Fixed* are pushed to this branch after this comment.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **Reproduced.** Copy a database that has no `settings` table (a pre-T23 backup) over `cms.db` while the server runs, and `/style.css` returns a 500. The server already set up that path, so it never creates the table, and every admin and preview page loses its styling until a restart. | **Fixed.** `theme.selected()` falls back to `default` when the table is missing. New test: `test_step2_a_database_without_the_settings_table_still_gets_a_stylesheet`. Saving a theme on such a database still needs a server restart first. |\n| 2 | `render_site` empties `site/` before it reads the theme. If that read fails, an empty `site/` is left behind, and `cms deploy` would push it. | **Fixed.** The theme's bytes are read before `site/` is cleared. New test: `test_step3_a_publish_that_cannot_read_the_theme_leaves_the_last_export_whole`. |\n| 3 | If `app/themes/default` itself is renamed, the fallback points at a missing file. | **Not changed.** `default` is the fallback by contract (`DEFAULT_THEME`, CONTEXT.md), and `test_step1` pins the folder names. Since fix 2, a missing default makes `cms publish` stop without touching `site/`. |\n| 4 | `stylesheet(name)` joins an unchecked name into a path. A future caller that passes request input could read outside `app/themes/`. | **Fixed.** `stylesheet()` no longer takes a name. Paths for named themes are private, and their names come only from `names()`. |\n| 5 | The saved banner says the public site changes on `cms publish`, but the live site also needs `cms deploy`. | **Fixed.** The banner and the route's docstring now name both steps. |\n| 6 | `/style.css` serves new bytes at the same URL after a switch, but sends no `Cache-Control`. | **Fixed.** It sends `Cache-Control: no-cache`, and a step 2 test asserts it. |\n| 7 | `test_access_control_sweep.py` still leaves out `/admin/settings` and `/admin/media`. | **Not changed** (same as S4 in round 1). That file existed at `mp2plus-base`. S1 comes next and builds the list from the router. |\n| 8 | `test_step1` demands exactly `[\"style.css\"]` in each folder, so a `.DS_Store` or `desktop.ini` would fail it. | **Fixed.** It now checks the folder's `.css` files only. |\n| 9 | Every `/style.css` request opens a database connection and scans the themes folder. | **Not changed.** That is the local admin console (ADR-001), never public. A cache would bring back the stale-theme risk that step 2's tests guard against. |\n| 10 | The chapter theme is a near-full copy of default, and the class-name test can't catch layout drift. | **Not changed** (round 1 S1). The spec asks for one CSS file per theme. The step 5 tests now check the exported layout at 390 px in both themes. A base-plus-tokens build would break \"compare `site/style.css` with the theme's file\". |\n| 11 | `--on-accent` is defined in chapter but never used. | **Fixed.** Removed. |\n| 12 | `CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE` now exists in a third module. | **Not changed** (round 1 S5). |\n| 13 | CLAUDE.md says the findings belong on the issue, but #23 had only a link. | **Fixed.** Both rounds' findings are now posted in full on #23 too. |\n\n**Evidence after the fixes:**\n- `tests/test_theme.py`: 32 passed.\n- Full suite: __FULL__ passed. The 367 tests that existed before are unchanged.\n- `check_submission.py --stage 2`: __CHECKER__.\n- Walk: __WALK__.\n- Mutations: 26/26 killed. The three new ones were: the read moved after `site/` is cleared, the missing-table fallback removed, and `no-cache` dropped.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

the same URL serves new\n  bytes after a switch.\n- theme.stylesheet() no longer takes a name; named paths are private\n  and come only from names().\n- The saved banner names both `cms publish` and `cms deploy`.\n- test_step1 checks a folder's .css files only, so .DS_Store or\n  desktop.ini can't fail it. chapter's unused --on-accent is removed.\n\ntests/test_theme.py: 32 passed; This decision was influenced by new information about grading that I received verbally from Professor Chun about needing to create a general CMS with a website built on top of it, rather than a specific type of CMS.\n< Other grill decisions I made were generally refinements of what the AI proposed, such as what Admin/Editor permissions should look like (such as that Editors should be able to delete content, I decided to add this because it can make using the CMS quicker instead of having to get admin permission each time, and anyone that edits a website should be trusted with the content) and what the CMS features should be. This is all verifiable with the transcripts and the CONTEXT.md file. The decision date for all this is 840feb9 on the 29th of September.\n< However, I built the custom, client-specific website for the Upper Arlington High School Computer Science Honor Society with client Dr. Diane Kahle in mind. I used the complete CMS to build it. I created two Posts on the \"/\" (main) page. One post is just a welcoming post, and the other is about an annual event that the CSHS chapter conducts, which is called Hour of Code. I created/expanded a computer science coursework page, the About page (which had everything from mission and why you should join to graduation awards) and also the Contact us page where I linked Dr. Diane Kahle's email. The website is live on GitHub pages. The commits were done to gh-pages and they are bce4dd6 and 5db2c46 (both on October 7th). Also, the title of the site is \"UAHS CSHS\", which just stands for Upper Arlington High School Computer Science Honor Society. I used the features that were built during the development phases of the CMS, and they worked correctly. The \"Hour of Code\" post was first written using the Editor account and then published using the admin account. I also used the revision history feature, specifically with 8 revisions and one roll back on the Contact Us page. The computer science coursework page had 3 revisions and the About page had 5 revisions. \n< * (b) The AI didn't necessarily make stuff up but it did drift from what the rubric requested during the /implement stage, such as when it didn't take into account that a .env.example should work properly when the commands get fired off. This was to be expected, because the model was a Sonnet 5 at Extra thinking effort but not as capable as Opus 5.5 High. The workflow caught it here in the sense that when I ran /code-review, as detailed in the README.md file, I switched to Opus 5.5 High and it immediately spotted a bunch of issues. It then subsequently asked about these errors, I confirmed that it should go fix them, and it fixed all the bugs and ran tests that successfully passed. This was ticket 10 (T10, issue #11), and it was at line 18 in /app/settings.py that \"load_dotenv\" was added. So /code-review was useful to make sure that I wasn't proceeding to push any commits with hallucinated and incorrect code. This is verifiable with the transcript specifically, as it shows how I ran /code-review and that the model flagged all those bugs. This is all at the commits e043236 (most issues weres solved in this one), 3334e8e and e9dfb18 on the 6th of October.\n< * (c) The skills I used were just the main workflow Matt Pocock skills, meaning /grill-with-docs, /to-spec, /to-tickets, /implement and /code-review. since those are the most applicable to this project. I used them because that's essentially the point of the project, and also, they make the AI SWE process very easy to go through because you can clarify what you want with the project and also steer the AI in a specific direction, and also it mitigates a lot of the issues of AI right now, such as context drift or hallucinations, etc. A prompt style I used a few times was telling the model to basically \"perform a gap analysis,\" which is where it compares the project against the rubric and manual and verifies if everything is correct or if I'm short on points. It is also useful because it lets me know exactly what the next steps should be to maximize points. A resource I used is the Claude Code documentation just to remind myself of what certain commands like /status and /context do. The pivot from a client-specific CMS to a general CMS with a client-specific website resulted in more planning time, but overall the idea was better aligned with what Professor Chun expects, which is why the switch was made.\n< * (d) Future improvements include improving the design of the CMS so it looks prettier, and including more features such as themes and templates for website designs. These would be useful to add, both for convenience when using the CMS (nicer layout) and to be able to build websites with more features. Additionally, one very important feature to add is media uploads such as adding images. This would make the CMS more useful for the client, Dr. Diane Kahle, who could then add pictures of events such as hackathons and hour of code, which would help promote the chapter better. It would also be an improvement to add an events calendar, so that it is easy to keep track of the latest events. This is all at the commits e043236 (most issues weres solved in this one), 3334e8e and e9dfb18 on the 6th of October.^M$\n* (c) The skills I used were just the main workflow Matt Pocock skills, meaning /grill-with-docs, /to-spec, /to-tickets, /implement and /code-review. since those are the most applicable to this project. I used them because that's essentially the point of the project, and also, they make the AI SWE process very easy to go through because you can clarify what you want with the project and also steer the AI in a specific direction, and also it mitigates a lot of the issues of AI right now, such as context drift or hallucinations, etc. A prompt style I used a few times was telling the model to basically \"perform a gap analysis,\" which is where it compares the project against the rubric and manual and verifies if everything is correct or if I'm short on points. It is also useful because it lets me know exactly what the next steps should be to maximize points. A resource I used is the Claude Code documentation just to remind myself of what certain commands like /status and /context do. The pivot from a client-specific CMS to a general CMS with a client-specific website resulted in more planning time, but overall the idea was better aligned with what Professor Chun expects, which is why the switch was made.^M$\n* (d) Future improvements include improving the design of the CMS so it looks prettier, and including more features such as themes and templates for website designs. These would be useful to add, both for convenience when using the CMS (nicer layout) and to be able to build websites with more features. Additionally, one very important feature to add is media uploads such as adding images. This would make the CMS more useful for the client, Dr. Diane Kahle, who could then add pictures of events such as hackathons and hour of code, which would help promote the chapter better. It would also be an improvement to add an events calendar, so that it is easy to keep track of the latest events. For now, the main page displays the latest posts, which is the only way to see the events.^M$\n^M$\nAdditionally, to explain the context threshold hook, it essentially keeps track of the context length with a percentage bar and the model being used, and at certain thresholds, it warns about the context length increasing, and then documents it by creating a row in the \"usage-ledger.csv\" file.^M$\n^M$\nAlso, I wanted to note a couple of things:^M$\n* The /implement process was sort of done in one go rather than in separate sessions. There were ticket blocks, but it wasn't done one session per ticket.^M$\n* There was also a Windows app alias issue, where when the hooks used to write new rows to the usage-ledger.csv file were activated, they called on python3 instead of python, and that didn't work for my system. Essentially there is a large gap that doesn't show the token usage during the implementation phase. ^M$\n* I added 3 screenshots displaying the revisions I made using the CMS, saved in /docs/screenshots.^M$\n^M$\nWith that said, here's the comparison between the token budget plan and the usage ledger^M$\n* The plan was to use about 20% on /grill-with-docs, /to-spec and /to-tickets, ^M$\n^M$\nbut that's not how it played out. This discrepancy makes sense because I had to do a big pivot from a client-specific wordpress CMS to a general wordpress CMS, which took more time with the grilling and rewriting the spec.^M$\n* The 5 hour context percentage got to 54%, which was when I was doing the extra credit tickets. The plan was to use 3% per ticket. There were only 2 tickets, T15 and T16, and they spent 6% and 18% of the 5 hour window respectively, which is over the budget, but it added well to the project and adds a safety margin to the project grade with the extra credit.^M$\n* The /code-review stage of the workflow chewed up a significant amount. At the point where I switched from Sonnet to Opus 5. High, as can be seen in the usage ledger, the 5 hour context percentage went up from 10% to 42%, because with my first run of Opus 5.5 High, I ran /code-review for the first time. However, since the run is actually 5 days apart, the /code-review was run on a fresh 5 hour context, which means that 42% of the window was taken up by that /code-review run alone. The ticket T10 was very heavy on token usage in particular, since it resolved multiple bugs at once. T11 took 13% of the 5 hour context limit. These all show that I've gone over-budget from the originally planned idea, which was to get abotu 3% per ticket. To avoid this in the future, it's best to get Opus 5.5 High (or better, xHigh) running for the /implement phase as well, so that /code-review doesn't have such increased token usage.^M$\n* Additionally, the extra credit tickets ended up filling a significant portion of both the context window and the 5 hour limit. The weekly limited was relatively untouched though. ^M$\n* This data shows me that the project required considerably more tokens that expected, and this is largely because of the pivot and the process of fixing bugs. Future budget plans should therefore include and take into account any potential unexpected bug fixing and project trajectory correction into the total token budget plan. {"parentUuid":"81f72f37-8650-414f-9d0a-13463b7c08ba","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgF2byziGvyZ6yqkqq4zY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01HwY9VQFeYWarKmtxRepw9f","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\mp2plus-handoff-07_s1-access-matrix_20261021.md","content":"# Handoff: MP2plus, F8/P1 done → next S1 (Direct-URL access matrix)\n\n**Written:** 2026-10-21, about 3:40am EDT\n**Repo:** `C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms` → https://github.com/Rajan-Thakur/iphs400-mp2-cms\n**Hard deadline:** tag `mp2plus-final` pushed and the email sent by **Wed 2026-10-21, 2:40pm EDT**. That's the end of the no-penalty grace. Points cap at +30.\n\n**Read first:**\n- `CLAUDE.md`\n- The project memory, especially `mp2plus.md`, `mp2-repo-reference.md` and `mp2-prose-is-human.md`. The index auto-loads.\n- The plan: `notes/mp2plus-plan.md`. The order is F1 ✅ → F5 ✅ → F8 via P1 ✅ → **S1**.\n- **S1 in the manual:** lines 614–648 of `git show template/main:docs/manual_iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_20261012.md`. It has the steps, the `/tdd` prompt, a 6-row acceptance table and \"If it goes wrong\". A copy is at `%TEMP%\\mp2plus_manual_20261012.md`.\n- **S1 in the rubric:** `git show template/main:docs/mp2plus-grading-rubric_20261012.md`, around line 263. Rows 2 and 3 together are the \"generated from the router\" tier.\n- The previous handoff, for F8/P1 context: `%TEMP%\\mp2plus-handoff-06_f8-p1-theme_20261021.md`.\n\n## State\n\n| Item | State |\n|---|---|\n| `main` = `origin/main` | `4a030e8` (the user's \"Added report rows\"), on top of the PR #24 merge `a2e75b6`. Working tree clean. |\n| F8 + P1 | Done. [#23](https://github.com/Rajan-Thakur/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/23) was closed by [PR #24](https://github.com/Rajan-Thakur/iphs400-mp2-cms/pull/24), merged at 07:26Z. The findings comments for both review rounds are on the PR and on the issue. |\n| Tests / checker | 399 pass (32 in `tests/test_theme.py`). `check_submission.py --stage 2`: 22/22. |\n| Report | `docs/iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_report_rajan-thakur_20261021.md` is committed and has rows for F1, F5, F8 and P1. **S1 needs its row added:** `\\| S1 \\| tests/test_access_matrix.py \\|`. |\n| `.claude/state/phase` | Still `T23`. **Run `echo S1 > .claude/state/phase` first.** S1 is a security exercise, so it uses its id, not an issue number, and it needs no issue. |\n| Real `cms.db` | It holds the client site: 7 items, 25 revisions. It was reseeded by accident at 06:49Z and restored from the scratchpad backup; its sha256 starts `7a17b571`. Back it up before anything drives a browser or a review fork. |\n\n## S1: what the manual asks\n\n- Use `/tdd` to write `tests/test_access_matrix.py`. The prompt is at manual lines 621–624. Build the app with `create_app()` and collect every admin-only route **from the router, through a marker in code**, never from a typed list.\n- For each route and method:\n  - `client_as(\"editor\")` gets 403 or a redirect.\n  - An anonymous client is redirected to `/login`.\n  - Path parameters are filled with seeded ids.\n- **Do not change existing tests.** The gate (rubric P0.4) allows existing test files to change by added lines only.\n- Step 3 is the judge's check: a throwaway admin-only route, \"marked the way your other admin routes are\", must be covered with no edit to the test.\n- Then commit with a message starting `S1:` and push. Ask the user who commits. For F8 they let me commit and push. Every commit must be authored by the student (gate, line 57); git config `Rajan Thakur` covers that.\n\n## The snag (decide with the user before coding)\n\nThere is **no shared marker today.** Every admin-only route depends on a per-route wrapper that calls `require_admin` inside, with its own refusal message. A router walk sees only the wrappers:\n\n| Wrapper (`Depends(...)`) | Where | Routes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `_require_admin_for_users` | `app/routes/users.py:58` | GET `/admin/users`, GET+POST `/admin/users/new`, POST `/admin/users/{user_id}/role`, POST `/admin/users/{user_id}/deactivate` |\n| `_require_admin_to_publish` | closure in `build_content_router`, `app/routes/content_crud.py:35` | POST `/admin/{posts,pages}/{item_id}/publish` and `/unpublish` |\n| `_require_admin_to_schedule` | same closure scope, `content_crud.py:38` | POST `/admin/{posts,pages}/{item_id}/schedule` and `/cancel-schedule` |\n| `_require_admin_for_settings` | `app/routes/admin_settings.py:26` | GET+POST `/admin/settings` |\n\nThat makes **15 route+method pairs**: 5 for users, 8 for content (posts and pages built from one factory), and 2 for settings.\n\n`require_admin(request, detail=None)` (`app/guards.py:66`) **can't be used directly as `Depends(require_admin)`.** FastAPI would expose `detail` as a query parameter, so a visitor could set the 403 page's text.\n\nOptions to put to the user:\n1. **A guard factory in `app/guards.py`**, for example `admin_only(detail)`, that returns a dependency and tags it, either with an attribute or by registering it in a set. Every wrapper above becomes one call to it. The test then keeps each dependency whose `call` carries the tag (`route.dependant.dependencies[*].call`). A new admin route written the same way is covered automatically, which is step 3. This changes app code only, and the existing refusal messages must stay word for word, because existing tests assert them.\n2. **Tag the existing wrappers in place**, for example with an `@admin_only` decorator that sets an attribute. The change is smaller, but the content closures need the decorator applied inside `build_content_router`.\n\nEither way, also check whether any marked route is missed: recurse into `dependant.dependencies`. Plan committed as 8ddb990 (`mp2plus: plan`): F1, F4, F5, F8. Base results: checker 22/22, 286 tests. Phase file says `revise`.\n\n**Decided 2026-10-20:** F4 dropped. Order is **F1 → F5 → F8 (carried by P1: branch `mp2plus-theme` + PR) → S1**, worth 9+7+7+6+6 = 35 raw, capped at 30. The user edited the plan to match and is recommitting it themselves. F1: `cms publish` copies **every** file in `media/` (the user's call: anything in `media/` is meant to be public), and the admin serves `/media/` to logged-in users so library thumbnails and the editor's preview work. P1: findings go on the PR, plus a one-line link on the issue.\n\n**F1 closed 2026-10-21 03:57Z:** the user committed and pushed `5cf2937` on top of `c755c3f`; #21 is closed with both findings comments above the close. Next is F5; the handoff is `%TEMP%\\mp2plus-handoff-05_f5-search_20261021.md`. Earlier history: issue #21, commit c755c3f. Findings comment is posted on #21. 343 tests pass (57 in `tests/test_media.py`), checker 22/22, screenshots committed. `tests/conftest.py` gained 2 lines (`settings.MEDIA` → tmp). The Alt text rule is a round trip through `render_markdown`, not a character list. A second /code-review round left 3 fixes **uncommitted** (invisible-only alt text, the backslash named in the message, partial-file cleanup; 352 tests). The round-2 findings comment is posted on #21. The user said \"Just don't do commits\": they commit and push themselves. Their `/code-review` prompt said #14/T14 by mistake (copied from the manual's example); it is #21. Still the user's to do: commit, push, the report row. Next issue number: #22.\n\n**F5 closed 2026-10-21 05:54Z** by the user's commit `50ff385` (pushed). **Next is F8 via P1.** The handoff is `%TEMP%\\mp2plus-handoff-06_f8-p1-theme_20261021.md`; the F8 issue will be #23 and the PR #24. History: issue #22, phase `T22`.\n- After two review rounds: 367 tests pass (15 in `tests/test_search.py`); checker 22/22; 24/24 mutations killed; walk 65/65; screenshots retaken.\n- The user picked the **dev-server HTTP seam only**, then OK'd two `cms publish` tests after review.\n- Both findings comments (round 1 and round 2) were posted on #22 at 05:33Z, with the user's OK. #22 stays open until the user's `T22: … Closes #22` commit. The user commits and pushes.\n- `search` is now in `RESERVED_SLUGS`. The new glossary terms are Search index and Excerpt.\n- **The built-in `/code-review` fork wrote two rows into the real `cms.db`.** Its `import *` of conftest skipped the `_isolated_seeded_db` fixture. It cleaned up and I verified the database. Warn about this before a review that drives a browser.\n- Next: F8 via P1.\n\n**F8 via P1, 2026-10-21 ~2:45am EDT:** issue #23, branch `mp2plus-f8` (the user's name, not `mp2plus-theme`), PR #24. The user let me commit, push and open the PR this time. I committed `6ed8624`, posted the findings comment on PR #24 at 06:44:02Z with a link on #23, then pushed `21917c0` (\"T23: … Closes #23\") at 06:44:13Z. **Still the user's to do: `gh pr merge 24 --merge --delete-branch`**, then `git switch main && git pull`, then check #23 is closed by the PR.\n- Results: 397 tests pass (30 in `tests/test_theme.py`); checker 22/22; walk 83/83 (scratchpad `walk_theme.py`); 23/23 mutations killed.\n- The user's decisions: the whole app follows the theme (`/style.css` serves the selected theme); the second theme is `chapter` (black and gold).\n- New code: `app/theme.py`, `app/routes/admin_settings.py` (guard is the wrapper `_require_admin_for_settings`, same S1 snag as below), and a `settings` table (key/value).\n- The real `cms.db` is unchanged and has no `settings` table yet; it is created on first open.\n- In T16 a commit with `Closes #18` inside PR #19 still recorded the PR as the closer.\n- **Round 2 (the user's built-in `/code-review`, 07:20Z):**\n  - Findings were posted on PR #24. Both rounds were also posted in full on #23, because CLAUDE.md wants them on the issue, not just a link.\n  - The fixes were pushed as `8597f45` at 07:20:38Z, after the comments.\n  - Results: 399 tests, checker 22/22, 26/26 mutations killed.\n- **The real `cms.db` was reseeded at 06:49:44Z from outside this session.** It matches the manual's `rm cms.db && seed_demo`. With the user's OK I restored it from the scratchpad backup (hash `7a17b571…`, 7 items / 25 revisions). The demo copy was kept in the scratchpad.\n- Two stray `python.exe` workers from 2026-10-16 old dev servers are still alive. They listen on no port.\n\n**S1 snag:** admin-only routes depend on wrapper closures (`_require_admin_to_publish`, `_require_admin_to_schedule` in `content_crud.py`, `_require_admin_for_users` in `users.py`) that call `require_admin` inside, so a router walk can't see `require_admin`. S1 needs a marker on those dependencies.\n\n**F4 conflict (flagged to the user):** T16 (#18) already shipped scheduled publishing, so F4 scores 0 (\"a feature already present at mp2plus-base is not scored again\"). F4's spec also clashes with T16's tests (`test_editors_see_no_schedule_controls`, the flip to Published in `test_scheduling.py`), and changing base test assertions fails the gate, which zeroes every exercise.\n\n**Rules that bite:** issue first (label `stretch`, body = acceptance table verbatim + `Blocked by: none`); phase `T<issue#>` set before the session; commit `T<issue#>: … Closes #<issue#>`; findings comment before close; tests in `tests/test_{slug}.py` named `test_step<k>_…`; screenshots `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-{slug}-{1280,390}.png`; base test files may only gain cases. Issues and PRs share numbering. `/mattpocock-skills:implement` works when invoked by name, even though the skill list doesn't show it.\n\n**Codebase facts:** since F8, the stylesheet is `app/themes/<name>/style.css`. `app.theme.stylesheet()` is read per request for `/style.css` and copied byte for byte by `render_site`.
